page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text; no marginal notes. Page number and running head at the top; catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: Apulei Celsi mirabilem antidotu non prę-terimus silentio, ob dotes maximas, qui-bus aduerfus hunc miserrimum morbum est prædica, quam nobis in hunc modu de-scripsit Scribonius Largus. Nardi Syriaci, croci, myrrhæ, cofti, calsiç, cinamomi, scæ-nu anthi, piperis albi, piperis longi, casto-rei, galbani, resinæ terebinthinæ, opij sin-gulorum *.P.iij. (Hæ notæ *.P. uel dena-rium unum, uel Græcam drachmam, quæ notabitur hoc signo. 3. significant.) alterci albi *.P.ij. anesi *.P. j.apij feminis, traga-canthi singulorum. *.P.fex. mellis attici sex-tarium unum, uini Falerni unciam. In hoc maceratur tragacanthum & opium pridie: Postero die contusis cæteris, miscentur in melle galbanum & resina, fictili patella su-per carbones impofita refoluuntur: dein-de arida asperguntur, & si opus est, adijci-tur mel: & ut cerati teneri spisitudine ha-beant, & rursus patella super igne impo-nitur, mouenturq; quæ sunt in ea, spatha fra-xinea. Coquitur medicamentu donec cro-cinum habeat colorem:ultima quæ sunt u-no macerata adijciuntur: uafe uitreo anti-dotus reponitur. Datur fabæ Ægyptiç ma-gnitudine ex aqua. Facit etiam ad stoma-chi

page.notes: The asterisk-and-letter marks such as *.P.iij. and *.P.ij. are printed in the text column, not in margins, so they stay inline. The first line of the page may continue a sentence from the previous page. The final word "stomachi" is cut off at the foot and only "chi" is visible as the catchword. Some letters in the lower lines are faint, including "spisitudine" and "fictili", and should be checked against the scan.
